resources.string: %1$s is playing on this TV now. Let %2$s play instead?
Connect the TV first, with the TV Settings Button.
The stick is on %1$s of the TV.
The TV did not say. Is it on, with this stick’s picture in front?

A phone that connects while the TV is off presses Home for you, which makes the stick ask the TV to switch on over HDMI-CEC (the TV needs its SimpLink or HDMI-CEC setting on, and the key service must be on). To be woken over the network as well, the TV needs: General, Devices, External Devices, TV On With Mobile, Turn On Via Wi-Fi.
Is this TV visible to phones?
This video cannot be played here

Pressing Menu twice opens a panel over the screen: scenes, input, picture mode, sound output, volume, screen off, a sleep timer and turning the TV off. A single press still opens the TV’s own settings, but waits a third of a second to see whether a second press follows. Switch this off and a single press acts at once.
Holding the Menu button does this. TV Off And Sleep counts three seconds first, and any key cancels it.

When the TV goes to the chosen input, its picture mode is set to the chosen one. The TV keeps one picture mode per input, so nothing is put back when you leave. It changes your TV’s picture settings, so it is off until you switch it on.
When a new song starts playing from your phone while you are in another app, a small card with the cover, title and artist appears for about 4 seconds. Off until you turn it on.

Play, pause, previous, next and volume for your phone’s music, over any app. Open it from the quick panel (it gets a Music Remote row), by holding Menu (choose Music Remote under TV Features, Hold Menu), or with OK while the glance card is up. Off until you turn it on.

A card with the time, date, weather and what is playing, for 4 seconds over any app. Show it by holding Menu: choose Glance Card under TV Features, Hold Menu. The weather comes from the TV Home launcher. Off until you turn it on.

Holding the Home button opens a list of the last five apps you used, so you can switch back. A normal press of Home works as always. It needs the menu button service to be on; while Hold Home is on, that service also notes which app comes to the front (nothing else). Off until you turn it on.

After the hour you choose, the TV’s OLED brightness is lowered, and put back in the morning if you have not changed it yourself. It changes your TV’s picture settings, so it stays off until you turn it on. It needs the TV connected (TV Features).
The hour the TV’s brightness is lowered.
The hour the TV’s brightness is put back.
How bright the OLED is at night, as a part of the TV’s scale. It is only ever lowered, never raised above what the TV had.

If nothing has been pressed or played for this long and the TV is showing this stick, the TV is warned for 2 minutes (any key cancels) and then turned off. It never acts while the TV shows another input, such as your PS5. It needs the TV connected and The Stick’s TV Input known (TV Features). Off until you choose a time.

While a text box is open on the TV, a link appears on the screen; open it on your phone and type there, and the text appears in the box. It works in apps whose search box is a standard Android text box; YouTube draws its own keyboard, which this cannot reach. It needs its own accessibility service, which you switch on once (the screen shows the commands). Off until you turn it on.

Type On Phone needs its own accessibility service. Run these two commands once from a computer (they keep what is already on):

%1$s

%2$s

Then the link appears whenever a text box opens on the TV.
Lets you type on your phone into a text box that is open on the TV. It only notices which text box is in focus and puts in the text you send; it does nothing unless you switched Type On Phone on.
Switch on Glance Card in Extras first
Switch on Music Remote in Extras first
Opens the quick panel with a double press of the Menu button. A single press still opens the TV’s own settings.
What holding the Menu button does: turn the TV off and let the stick sleep, open the quick panel, apply the Game scene, show the glance card, or open the music remote. Off until you choose one.
What each scene does: the input, picture mode, sound output, a volume that is only ever lowered, and the screen.
Short notices at the top of the screen for what the stick does to the TV: a scene, a sleep timer, a picture mode.
Whether the stick is connected to your LG TV. Connect it with the TV Settings Button.
When a phone starts playing while the TV is off, the stick wakes it.
Which input of the TV this stick is on, learned while the TV shows this stick.
While only music plays, the TV’s screen goes off (the sound goes on) and comes back at the next key.
The phone’s music pauses when the TV is switched to another input or turned off.
The phone’s volume slider moves the TV’s own volume: 100% is the TV’s 100, within the Volume Limits.
Forgets the TV: its pairing, address and input.
